diagrams.title: The Two-Contract Double Close Sequence
diagrams.subtitle: Two contracts, two independent closings, the end buyer's cash in escrow first
diagrams.caption: Wholesalers, title operators and transactional lenders run the same five moves so the seller never sees the resale price and the end buyer never sees the buy price.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Fees shown are the quoted rates of Flip Lab Capital (1% to 3% of purchase) and Bright Closings (1% plus $100 above $75,000, flat $850 below). Practitioners split on whether leg one must close with outside cash or with the end buyer's wire.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Jerry Norton (Flipping Mastery TV), Ricky (Flip Lab), Jasper Cool, Ryan Schrope and Game Changer Real Estate Insights.

stages.label: Lock the cash buyer deposit
stages.detail: Jerry Norton requires a $2,500 minimum non-refundable deposit, $5,000 to $10,000 preferred, backed by a release clause needing no further escrow instruction.

stages.label: Write the closer into both contracts
stages.detail: Insert 'seller or buyer agrees to use the closing services of' plus an investor-friendly title company, because the wrong title company will kill the deal.

stages.label: Screen REO and short sale deed limits
stages.detail: Game Changer Real Estate Insights checks bank-owned and short sale deeds for resale bans of 30, 60 or 90 days before promising a double close.

stages.label: Confirm end buyer cash in escrow
stages.detail: Flip Lab funds only after title confirms the end buyer's funds are there; Ryan Schrope moves no money on the A leg until B-to-C funds land.

stages.label: Fund leg A and repay from leg B-to-C
stages.detail: Funder wires the A-to-B purchase and is repaid on the B-to-C leg, often within an hour; a $100,000 purchase at Bright Closings costs $1,100 out of the second closing.

diagrams.title: Soft Proof of Funds Acceptance Funnel
diagrams.subtitle: How listing agents respond to a soft letter, and what operators do with holdouts
diagrams.caption: Across 20 years of the agent model, Jerry Norton reports about 90% of agents accept a soft letter; the remaining holdouts get a contingency or a downgraded offer.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Values are normalized to 100 offers using Norton's about 90% versus about 10% split. Stages 4 and 5 are two competing practitioner responses to the same holdout group, not further attrition.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Jerry Norton (Flipping Mastery TV), Steph Davis (FlipThisWholesaler), Brent Daniels (Wholesaling Inc) and Foreclosure University.

stages.label: Offers backed by a soft proof letter
stages.detail: Letters from local hard money lenders or Tailwind at $1.99 each or $9.99 a month; the name on the proof must match the name on the offer.

stages.label: Listing agent accepts the soft letter
stages.detail: Norton says a soft letter checks the box for most listing agents.

stages.label: Holdouts demanding hard proof
stages.detail: Agents tie bank statements to the buyer named on the offer.

stages.label: Holdouts given a 5-7 day contingency
stages.detail: Norton offers the contingency and fires agents who still reject soft letters.

stages.label: Holdouts moved to a financed offer
stages.detail: Steph Davis still makes the offer but uses a financing contingency.

diagrams.title: Tennessee No-Money Wholesale Net
diagrams.subtitle: $38,000 A-to-B purchase resold at $72,900 with transactional funding
diagrams.caption: Dave Dinkel's deal netted $30,070.71 at 1% plus a $50 wire fee, with $39,727.93 of transactional funding covering the buy and no earnest money from the investor.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The 1% fee is applied to the $39,727.93 funded amount. Remaining closing costs are the residual between the reported spread and the reported net, not a separately itemized figure.

diagrams.title: What a Double Close Costs Versus an Assignment
diagrams.subtitle: Funding fees, closing hits and the spread where operators switch
diagrams.caption: Assignment is the cheap default exit; operators switch to a double close only when the spread is fat enough to absorb two closings and a funding fee.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Where no single figure was cited, the typical marker is the range midpoint. The switch point spans Lex Levinrad at $10,000, Brent Daniels at $15,000 and Jamil Damji at $20,000.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Michael (The Virtual Investor), Brent Daniels (Wholesaling Inc), David Olds REI, Jamil Damji and Lex Levinrad.

bars.label: Profit lost to title on a double close

diagrams.title: Earnest Money Protection Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Neutral holder, verified wire, seasoned cash, live contingency
diagrams.caption: The deposit is only recoverable through a live, written contingency; miss a date or waive a clause and the money is exposed.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order follows the deposit's path from funding to closing. The 60-day seasoning rule applies to conventional, FHA, USDA and Fannie- and Freddie-backed loans.
diagrams.note: Attributed to The Treasure Valley Home Show, Larry Mastropieri, Charles Nedder, Katie Anderson, Yanowitz Law Firm and Andrew Finney Team.

nodes.question: Is the deposit going to a neutral holder such as title, a brokerage trust account or attorney escrow?
nodes.fail_action: Do not send it; in Connecticut both attorneys must agree to release the funds.

nodes.question: Did the wire instructions come directly from the title company and get confirmed by your own call?
nodes.fail_action: Stop and call title yourself; intercepted funds are gone.

nodes.question: Has the cash sat in the bank account for 60 days?
nodes.fail_action: Treat it as non-sourceable; the closing credit can be backed out.

nodes.question: Is a written contingency still live, with cancellation by day 9 or 10 of a 10-day inspection period?
nodes.pass_next: Deposit stays recoverable and becomes a closing credit.
nodes.fail_action: Deposit is exposed; a buyer cancelling out of compliance loses it to the seller.

diagrams.title: Exit-First Bridge and Credit Line Architecture
diagrams.subtitle: Short-term, equity-sized debt underwritten on the sale or refinance
diagrams.caption: Every bridge loan has an exit, and the lender asks about it before almost anything else; each capital route around it is priced and capped differently.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Leverage caps conflict across practitioners, from 70% to 80% combined LTV. Line of credit costs assume interest only on a $20K draw from a $50K line over 6 months.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Michael Daniel Investments, SEI Mortgage (Ryan Marks), Easy Lending USA, Rene Nelson, Fast Business Lending and The Mortgage Man (Steve Ferguson).

center.focus: Primary exit plus a second exit matched to slow or hot market conditions

spokes.kpi: 70% to 80% combined LTV over 6 to 12 months; SEI caps at 75%
75% at 2+ deals and FICO 620+, 72.5% at 1 deal, 70% new; 12 to 18 months
11% to 12%, not index-tied; interest-only about 1% of balance per month
About $583 at a bank vs $1,800 to $3,488 online on a $20K draw

diagrams.title: Title-Side Fee Hygiene
diagrams.subtitle: What title bills, what it costs, and what an operator can claw back
diagrams.caption: Rick treats the lien search as highly negotiable and asks for the reissue credit on every double close; Jerry Norton locks the cash buyer with a $5,000 non-refundable deposit.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Buckets are independent line items, not a summed closing statement. The reissue credit range applies the 50 to 55% discount to the $2,000 policy example.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Rick (Flip With Rick) and Jerry Norton (Flipping Mastery TV).
diagrams.total_range: $50 to $5,000 per line item on a $25,000 assignment deal

buckets.label: Lien search actual title cost
buckets.notes: Rick keeps the written report in every file as proof if liens surface later.

buckets.label: Lien search as billed
buckets.notes: The gap over actual cost is the negotiating room.

buckets.label: Reissue credit on a $2,000 policy
buckets.notes: 50 to 55% off the second-side policy, offered only when asked.

buckets.label: Cash buyer non-refundable deposit
buckets.notes: Posted at title on a $206,000 contract assigned at $231,000.

diagrams.title: 0% Business Credit Stack Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Personal file first, Chase next, sequenced banks, exit written before deployment
diagrams.caption: The stack is won or lost on the personal file; one 0% round on a fresh entity runs about $100K on average and about $225K at the top end.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels order the practitioner gates into a sequence; no practitioner reported a four-week calendar. Bank count splits from three to four up to eleven.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Colin Matthew, Jack McColl (BetterWealth), HowToCredit, Cal Barton, Marvin Francois and Gap Funding.

weeks.title: Audit the personal credit profile
weeks.deliverable: 680 minimum, 720-plus preferred, utilization near 10%, two or fewer recent inquiries
weeks.gate: Under three hard inquiries on every bureau

weeks.title: Apply at Chase first
weeks.deliverable: Ink Unlimited at $30-40K plus Ink Preferred at $40-60K for $70-100K at Chase
weeks.gate: Confirm the 0% covers purchases, balance transfers or both

weeks.title: Sequence the remaining banks
weeks.deliverable: Chase then US Bank; ask Navy Federal and PNC for multiple cards on one hard pull
weeks.gate: Stop at three to four banks or run up to eleven

weeks.title: Deploy with the exit written first
weeks.deliverable: Liquidate at 2.5% to about 6% depending on the route
weeks.gate: Borrow only what could be repaid within six months if the deal stalls
